lines.before: - **Never hand the owner a command an agent may run;** run it. On a permission block, ask in the thread for one typed sentence: a card tap does not clear the permission system, typed words do.
lines.after: - **Never hand the owner a command an agent may run;** run it. On a permission block, ask with the choice pop-up, the question quoting the exact act: the owner's tap clears it. Typed words only where the tool or model has no pop-up.
lines.why: K43 (the owner, 2026-11-13): the owner's yes is a pop-up tap, the standard in the kit and in every project that uses it

lines.before: **Hard rules:** batch at G3 (triage and diagnose everything, then fix roots). **One sweep:** one large sweep per branch; every fix ships with a test that fails before it, guard and permission fixes too; CI runs the full suite and auto-fix handles red. A second pass is the owner's call; escapes are measured next build. A finding carries to the next run only at medium or below: a high or critical is fixed before the PR (found after it: on the open PR), or the owner accepts it.
lines.after: **Hard rules:** batch at G3 (triage and diagnose everything, then fix roots). **One sweep:** one large sweep per branch; a fix that changes behaviour ships with a test that fails before it (rule:test-value); CI runs the full suite and auto-fix handles red. A second pass is the owner's call; escapes are measured next build. Findings are fixed in the build that finds them, low and medium too; a high or critical is fixed before the PR (found after it: on the open PR). What cannot be finished carries only on the owner's yes, first next build.
lines.why: the owner, 2026-11-13: nothing small rolls over, and a test is owed only where a fix changes behaviour

lines.before: **Mandatory for every feature and bugfix,** presentational, config and route-shell code included: RED (a failing test for the smallest behaviour, failing for the right reason - a compiling stub, not a 404 or type error) -> GREEN (minimum code) -> REFACTOR. Never defer the testable slice; a plan note deferring a test covers only parts needing unbuilt pieces - else surface the fork to the owner. Why: a test written after the code tests the code, not the requirement.
lines.after: **Mandatory for every change in behaviour** (a feature, a bugfix), presentational, config and route-shell code included; a change with no behaviour in it (wording, docs, a removal) owes no new test (rule:test-value): RED (a failing test for the smallest behaviour, failing for the right reason - a compiling stub, not a 404 or type error) -> GREEN (minimum code) -> REFACTOR. Never defer the testable slice; a plan note deferring a test covers only parts needing unbuilt pieces - else surface the fork to the owner. Why: a test written after the code tests the code, not the requirement.
lines.why: the owner, 2026-11-13: the test-first rule matches the newer bar for a new test (rule:test-value)

lines.before: The guard and the pre-push hook hold the bound, scan each pushed commit for secrets and log it; a held push names the limit it hit.
lines.after: The guard and the pre-push hook hold the bound, scan each pushed commit for secrets and log it; a refused push names the limit it hit.
lines.why: C17 (the 1.26.0 sweep): "Held" is one of the four kinds of refusal, so the plain verb is not used for another kind

lines.before: - **Hard rules (outward-facing):** ASCII; no AI / agent / tool references (reviews described BY DIMENSION + verdict); no links to gitignored vault docs; title `type: subject` (the squash subject, <= 72, CI checks it), H1 `<Area>: <line>` ending in it.
lines.after: - **Hard rules (outward-facing):** ASCII; no AI / agent / tool references (reviews described BY DIMENSION + verdict); no links to gitignored vault docs; title `type: subject` (squash subject + " (#n)" <= 72, CI checks), H1 `<Area>: <line>` ending in it.
lines.why: K37 (the 1.28.0 sweep): the PR title counts its squash suffix

lines.before: 2. **Sweep findings are fixed in their PR**, not only the easy ones; defer only the trivial (info, cosmetic, rare path, no harm), each recorded. Leftovers and post-PR findings at medium or below go to the handoff's carry-overs for the next focus build.
lines.after: 2. **Sweep findings are fixed in their PR**, the small ones too. A post-PR finding is fixed in the build that finds it; what carries (the rule above) goes to the handoff's carry-overs.
lines.why: the owner, 2026-11-13: nothing small rolls over, so no finding is deferred as trivial
